name: directory.list
description: List the entries in a directory. Returns name / type / size / timestamps / flags per entry. Read-only. Pass `recursive: true` for a subtree walk; pass `pattern` to filter by name; pass `limit` to cap the result count.

recursive.description: If true, walk the subtree depth-first and include descendants. Reparse points (junctions/symlinks) are NOT followed — they appear as `link`-type entries but the agent does not descend into them.

pattern.description: Optional name filter. Glob-style pattern (`*`, `?`) matched against each entry's name. Omit to include all entries.

limit.description: Optional cap on the returned entry count. Walk halts when the limit is reached. Omit for no cap.

name.description: Entry's filename (not full path) when `recursive: false`. When `recursive: true`, this is the path relative to the walk root with forward-slashes.

type.description: `file` for regular files; `directory` for subdirectories; `link` for reparse points / symlinks / junctions; `other` for devices / pipes / sockets.

size.description: Byte size. Zero for directories. Symlink size is the target's size when resolvable.

mtime_unix_s.description: Modification time as Unix epoch seconds.

ctime_unix_s.description: Creation time as Unix epoch seconds. (Windows tracks creation time per-file; Unix systems may report ctime as inode-change time instead.)

atime_unix_s.description: Access time as Unix epoch seconds. Many Windows configurations disable atime updates (NtfsDisableLastAccessUpdate); the value may equal mtime when atime is not maintained.

flags.description: Win32 FILE_ATTRIBUTE_* flags currently set. Per issue #93 — zero-cost set sourced from WIN32_FIND_DATA. Cloud-file flags (recall_on_*) are Windows 10+; older Windows omits them.

x-implementations.name: find_first_file_w
x-implementations.description: Win32 `FindFirstFileW` + `FindNextFileW` loop. Each iteration's WIN32_FIND_DATA carries name, attributes, size, all three timestamps — the full per-entry payload in one call per entry. Recursive walks issue a fresh FindFirstFileW per descended directory; pattern matching applies after each entry is materialised.

x-implementations.name: find_first_file_a
x-implementations.description: Win32 `FindFirstFileA` legacy fallback for NT 4 / 9x where FindFirstFileW is unavailable. ANSI names transcoded to UTF-8 by the agent.

windows-modern.description: FindFirstFileW + FindNextFileW. UTF-16 native, transcoded to UTF-8 for the wire. Long-path `\\?\` prefix automatic when input exceeds MAX_PATH. Cloud-file flags (recall_on_data_access, recall_on_open) populated for OneDrive / Files-On-Demand / Dropbox-shell-extension entries on Win 10+. Recursive walks respect `limit` precisely (halt mid-walk when reached).

windows-classic.description: FindFirstFileW / FindNextFileW on NT 5+; FindFirstFileA / FindNextFileA on NT 4 / 9x. No long-path support pre-NT-5.1. No cloud-file flags pre-Win-10. atime updates may be unreliable on FAT volumes — the agent reports the OS-supplied value regardless.
